## Projects (Detailed)

### 1. FlowCMS
- **Description**: Headless CMS with a visual block editor built with Next.js and Prisma. Designed for creating and managing content with ease.
- **URL**: https://kapiljangid.pro/projects/flowcms
- **GitHub**: https://github.com/kjxcodez/flowcms
- **Tech Stack**: Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Prisma, PostgreSQL
- **Key Features**: Drag-and-drop block editor, roles & permissions, API key generation, rich content schema builder, media library.

### 2. Rune Lang
- **Description**: A custom, interpreted programming language written entirely in TypeScript to understand compilers, interpreters, and ASTs.
- **URL**: https://kapiljangid.pro/projects/rune-lang
- **GitHub**: https://github.com/kjxcodez/rune-lang
- **Tech Stack**: TypeScript, Node.js
- **Key Features**: Custom lexer, parser, abstract syntax tree (AST) generator, and tree-walk interpreter. Supports variables, control flow, functions, and closures.

### 3. AI Auto Commit
- **Description**: CLI tool that generates conventional commit messages using AI by analyzing git diffs.
- **URL**: https://kapiljangid.pro/projects/ai-auto-commit
- **GitHub**: https://github.com/kjxcodez/ai-auto-commit
- **Tech Stack**: Node.js, TypeScript, Gemini API
- **Key Features**: Automated git diff analysis, generates conventional commits, interactive prompt, quick configuration.

### 4. Percept UI
- **Description**: An accessible, unstyled, and highly customizable React component library designed with Tailwind CSS integration in mind.
- **URL**: https://kapiljangid.pro/projects/percept-ui
- **GitHub**: https://github.com/kjxcodez/percept-ui
- **Tech Stack**: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
- **Key Features**: WAI-ARIA compliant, keyboard navigation out of the box, lightweight, modular imports.

### 5. Rune Lang VSCode

- **GitHub**: https://github.com/kjxcodez/rune-lang-vscode

## Blog Posts (Full Text & Summaries)

### 1. Building Products Taught Me More Than Tutorials Did
- **Date**: 2026-03-06
- **Link**: https://kapiljangid.pro/blog/building-products-taught-me-more-than-tutorials-did
- **Key Takeaways**:
  * Tutorials present a perfect, controlled environment where everything is predictable and goes according to plan.
  * Real products force you to think about edge cases, late or failed webhooks, authentication expiration, page refreshes, and API failures.
  * Developing a product requires thinking in terms of end-to-end workflows rather than just adding isolated features.
  * Debugging is one of the greatest teachers because it forces you to understand data flow, state management, and architectural decisions.
  * Rewriting code or shifting design decisions is a natural part of the learning and product-building process.

### 2. My Biggest Development Mistake: Building Too Much Before Validation
- **Date**: 2026-03-13
- **Link**: https://kapiljangid.pro/blog/my-biggest-development-mistake
- **Key Takeaways**:
  * More features do not automatically equal more value or utility.
  * In the early stages of a project, it's easy to waste time implementing features that users have not asked for (e.g., advanced role systems, complex analytics, future monetizations).
  * Building feels productive, but it can increase future maintenance weight and obscure the core problem being solved.
  * The portfolio redesign is an example: instead of building five separate websites for different modes, a single portfolio with multiple interchangeable visual experiences (modes) was cleaner and less complex.
  * Removing features is a deliberate design decision that drives focus and clarity.

### 3. The Problem With Side Projects: Finishing Is Harder Than Starting
- **Date**: 2026-04-26
- **Link**: https://kapiljangid.pro/blog/the-problem-with-side-projects-finishing-is-harder-than-starting
- **Key Takeaways**:
  * Starting a new project brings excitement and immediate gratification. Finishing a project, however, requires pushing through the "boring" final 10% (bugs, deployment, edge cases, responsiveness).
  * Setting a tight MVP (Minimum Viable Product) scope is essential for ever shipping a side project.

### 4. Things I Underestimated While Building a Headless CMS
- **Date**: 2026-05-17
- **Link**: https://kapiljangid.pro/blog/things-i-underestimated-while-building-a-headless-cms
- **Key Takeaways**:
  * Building a headless CMS involves complex data modeling, dynamic schema validations, block editor state management, and asset/media handling.
  * Scaling content delivery APIs globally requires careful caching, invalidation strategies, and robust error handling.

### 5. Why I Built a Programming Language Just to Understand Programming Better
- **Date**: 2026-05-26
- **Link**: https://kapiljangid.pro/blog/why-i-built-a-programming-language-just-to-understand-programming-better
- **Key Takeaways**:
  * Building Rune Lang demystified compilers and interpreters.
  * Writing a lexer, a parser, and a tree-walk interpreter taught the mechanics of tokenization, AST generation, environment scopes, and closures.
